507:     fn renumber_capture_indices(hir: Hir) -> Result<Hir, Error> {
508:         Ok(match hir.into_kind() {
509:             HirKind::Empty => Hir::empty(),
510:             HirKind::Literal(hir::Literal(lit)) => Hir::literal(lit),
511:             HirKind::Class(cls) => Hir::class(cls),
512:             HirKind::Look(x) => Hir::look(x),
513:             HirKind::Repetition(mut x) => {
514:                 x.sub = Box::new(Self::renumber_capture_indices(*x.sub)?);
515:                 Hir::repetition(x)
516:             }
517:             HirKind::Capture(mut cap) => {
518:                 cap.index = match cap.index.checked_add(1) {
519:                     Some(index) => index,
520:                     None => {
521:                         let msg =
522:                             "could not renumber capture index, too big";
523:                         return Err(Error::any(msg));
524:                     }
525:                 };
526:                 cap.sub = Box::new(Self::renumber_capture_indices(*cap.sub)?);
527:                 Hir::capture(cap)
528:             }
529:             HirKind::Concat(subs) => {
530:                 let subs = subs
531:                     .into_iter()
532:                     .map(Self::renumber_capture_indices)
533:                     .collect::<Result<Vec<Hir>, Error>>()?;
534:                 Hir::concat(subs)
535:             }
536:             HirKind::Alternation(subs) => {
537:                 let subs = subs
538:                     .into_iter()
539:                     .map(Self::renumber_capture_indices)
540:                     .collect::<Result<Vec<Hir>, Error>>()?;
541:                 Hir::alternation(subs)
542:             }
543:         })
544:     }

667:     fn extract(&self, hir: &Hir) -> TSeq {
668:         use regex_syntax::hir::HirKind::*;
669: 
670:         match *hir.kind() {
671:             Empty | Look(_) => TSeq::singleton(hir::literal::Literal::exact(vec![])),
672:             Literal(hir::Literal(ref bytes)) => {
673:                 let mut seq =
674:                     TSeq::singleton(hir::literal::Literal::exact(bytes.to_vec()));
675:                 self.enforce_literal_len(&mut seq);
676:                 seq
677:             }
678:             Class(hir::Class::Unicode(ref cls)) => {
679:                 self.extract_class_unicode(cls)
680:             }
681:             Class(hir::Class::Bytes(ref cls)) => {
682:                 self.extract_class_bytes(cls)
683:             }
684:             Repetition(ref rep) => self.extract_repetition(rep),
685:             Capture(hir::Capture { ref sub, .. }) => self.extract(sub),
686:             Concat(ref hirs) => self.extract_concat(hirs.iter()),
687:             Alternation(ref hirs) => self.extract_alternation(hirs.iter()),
688:         }
689:     }

691:     fn extract_concat<'a, I: Iterator<Item = &'a Hir>>(&self, it: I) -> TSeq {
692:         let mut seq = TSeq::singleton(hir::literal::Literal::exact(vec![]));
693:         let mut prev: Option<TSeq> = None;
694:         for hir in it {
695:             if seq.is_inexact() {
696:                 if seq.is_empty() {
697:                     return seq;
698:                 }
699:                 if self.seq_is_really_good(&seq) {
700:                     return seq;
701:                 }
702:                 prev = Some(match prev {
703:                     None => seq,
704:                     Some(prev) => self.seq_choose(prev, seq),
705:                 });
706:                 seq = TSeq::singleton(hir::literal::Literal::exact(vec![]));
707:                 seq.make_not_prefix();
708:             }
709:             seq = self.cross(seq, self.extract(hir));
710:         }
711:         if let Some(prev) = prev {
712:             self.seq_choose(prev, seq)
713:         } else {
714:             seq
715:         }
716:     }

718:     fn extract_alternation<'a, I: Iterator<Item = &'a Hir>>(
719:         &self,
720:         it: I,

723:         for hir in it {
724:             if !seq.is_finite() {
725:                 break;
726:             }
727:             seq = self.union(seq, &mut self.extract(hir));
728:         }
729:         seq

732:     fn extract_repetition(&self, rep: &hir::Repetition) -> TSeq {
733:         let mut subseq = self.extract(&rep.sub);
734:         match *rep {
735:             hir::Repetition { min: 0, max, greedy, .. } => {
736:                 if max != Some(1) {
737:                     subseq.make_inexact();
738:                 }
739:                 let mut empty = TSeq::singleton(hir::literal::Literal::exact(vec![]));
740:                 if !greedy {
741:                     std::mem::swap(&mut subseq, &mut empty);
742:                 }
743:                 self.union(subseq, &mut empty)
744:             }
745:             hir::Repetition { min, max: Some(max), .. } if min == max => {
746:                 assert!(min > 0);
747:                 let limit =
748:                     u32::try_from(self.extract_limit_repeat).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
749:                 let mut seq = TSeq::singleton(hir::literal::Literal::exact(vec![]));
750:                 for _ in 0..std::cmp::min(min, limit) {
751:                     if seq.is_inexact() {
752:                         break;
753:                     }
754:                     seq = self.cross(seq, subseq.clone());
755:                 }
756:                 if usize::try_from(min).is_err() || min > limit {
757:                     seq.make_inexact();
758:                 }
759:                 seq
760:             }
761:             hir::Repetition { min, max: Some(max), .. } if min < max => {
762:                 assert!(min > 0);
763:                 let limit =
764:                     u32::try_from(self.extract_limit_repeat).unwrap_or(u32::MAX);
765:                 let mut seq = TSeq::singleton(hir::literal::Literal::exact(vec![]));
766:                 for _ in 0..std::cmp::min(min, limit) {
767:                     if seq.is_inexact() {
768:                         break;
769:                     }
770:                     seq = self.cross(seq, subseq.clone());
771:                 }
772:                 seq.make_inexact();
773:                 seq
774:             }
775:             hir::Repetition { .. } => {
776:                 subseq.make_inexact();
777:                 subseq
778:             }
779:         }
780:     }

832:     fn cross(&self, mut seq1: TSeq, mut seq2: TSeq) -> TSeq {
833:         if !seq2.prefix {
834:             return self.seq_choose(seq1, seq2);
835:         }
836:         if seq1
837:             .max_cross_len(&seq2)
838:             .map_or(false, |len| len > self.extract_limit_total)
839:         {
840:             seq2.make_infinite();
841:         }
842:         seq1.cross_forward(&mut seq2);
843:         assert!(seq1.len().map_or(true, |x| x <= self.extract_limit_total));
844:         self.enforce_literal_len(&mut seq1);
845:         seq1
846:     }

848:     fn union(&self, mut seq1: TSeq, seq2: &mut TSeq) -> TSeq {
849:         if seq1
850:             .max_union_len(seq2)
851:             .map_or(false, |len| len > self.extract_limit_total)
852:         {
853:             seq1.keep_first_bytes(4);
854:             seq2.keep_first_bytes(4);
855:             seq1.dedup();
856:             seq2.dedup();
857:             if seq1
858:                 .max_union_len(seq2)
859:                 .map_or(false, |len| len > self.extract_limit_total)
860:             {
861:                 seq2.make_infinite();
862:             }
863:         }
864:         seq1.union(seq2);
865:         assert!(seq1.len().map_or(true, |x| x <= self.extract_limit_total));
866:         seq1
867:     }

873:     fn seq_is_good(&self, seq: &TSeq) -> bool {
874:         if self.seq_has_poisonous_literal(seq) {
875:             return false;
876:         }
877:         let Some(min) = seq.min_literal_len() else { return false };
878:         let Some(len) = seq.len() else { return false };
879:         if min <= 1 {
880:             return len <= 3;
881:         }
882:         min >= 2 && len <= 64 && len <= self.extract_limit_total
883:     }

886:         if self.seq_has_poisonous_literal(seq) {

889:         let Some(min) = seq.min_literal_len() else { return false };
890:         let Some(len) = seq.len() else { return false };
891:         min >= 3 && len <= 8 && len <= self.extract_limit_total

895:         let Some(lits) = seq.literals() else { return false };

897:             return true;

902:     fn seq_choose(&self, seq1: TSeq, seq2: TSeq) -> TSeq {
903:         if !seq1.is_finite() {
904:             return seq2;
905:         } else if !seq2.is_finite() {
906:             return seq1;
907:         }
908:         if self.seq_has_poisonous_literal(&seq1) {
909:             return seq2;
910:         } else if self.seq_has_poisonous_literal(&seq2) {
911:             return seq1;
912:         }
913:         let Some(min1) = seq1.min_literal_len() else { return seq2 };
914:         let Some(min2) = seq2.min_literal_len() else { return seq1 };
915:         if min1 < min2 {
916:             return seq2;
917:         } else if min2 < min1 {
918:             return seq1;
919:         }
920:         let len1 = seq1.len().unwrap();
921:         let len2 = seq2.len().unwrap();
922:         if len1 < len2 {
923:             return seq2;
924:         } else if len2 < len1 {
925:             return seq1;
926:         }
927:         if len1 > self.extract_limit_total {
928:             return seq2;
929:         }
930:         seq1
931:     }

1188:         //     (^|\W)(<original regex>)(\W|$)

1191:         // easy/common case, the original regex will be sandwiched between
1192:         // two codepoints that are in the \W class. So our approach here is to

part.text: All 22 test suites pass in the eval container as well. Final diff:

Fixed. The bug was in the `fast_find` fast path of `WordMatcher` (crates/regex/src/word.rs:1211).

**Root cause:** With `-w`, the word regex is `(^|\W)(pattern)(\W|$)`. The `fast_find` optimization assumed the full match was always sandwiched between two `\W` characters, so it blindly stripped the first and last characters to recover the pattern match. But for `some.domain.com/x`, the full match `some.domain.com/` used the `^` prefix alternative — so the first char `s` is a *word* character. Stripping it produced the wrong match `ome.domain.com`, and since `original.is_match("ome.domain.com")` succeeded, the bad result was returned.

**Fix** (mirrors upstream ripgrep PR #2576 for issue #2574): decode the characters at both ends of the full match; if either is a word character (meaning `^`/`$` matched rather than `\W`), bail out and defer to the slower capture-based engine, which is always correct.

Verified:
- The issue reproduction now prints `some.domain.com` for all three lines
- Existing word semantics preserved (`-2` still matches in `abc -2 bar` with `-w`, unlike `\b`)
- Full `cargo test --workspace` passes locally (all 22 test binaries) and in the eval container, including the `grep-regex` word tests and regression tests
